rv.q: Leaves you dizzy … Australian director Kip Williams turns Genet’s psychodrama into a dazzling digital-age headrush … You could say that this take on Jean Genet’s 1947 psychodrama of theatrical, erotic and murderous fantasy was A Lot. You might even think it was A Bit Much. But babe, you’d be wrong.

If you're prepared to surrender, it's a wild ride … This adaptation of Jean Genet’s play by Kip Williams makes use of phones to project the fantasy world of two sisters wishing to murder a terrible mistress but the true power is in the performances … In Australian auteur Kip Williams’s version, adapted and updated to a world of Instagram...

Dorian Gray’s Kip Williams dazzles again with feverish fantasy … There are superb performances in this screen-saturated staging of Jean Genet’s play, updated for the influencer age … Screens feature just as extravagantly in this three-hander that sweeps you into its turbulence at relentless speed. … Written and directed by Williams, this new...

Jean Genet’s drama becomes a vicious satire of the TikTok age … The Australian director Kip Williams brings a queasy contemporaneity to the suffocating 1947 play … Political metaphor, erotic fantasy, quasi-religious ceremony, it’s still a troubling, provocative watch.

Like being locked in a cupboard with Katie Price … Kip Williams’s manic revival of Jean Genet’s psychodrama is packed with clever effects but does nothing to solve the play’s mysteries … The set is the winner in this manic update of Jean Genet’s psychodrama, a Gallic exercise in demented role-playing, now given a modern influencer gloss by that...

Hotly-tipped Aussie director Kip Williams’s live video-centric take on the Jean Genet classic is gloriously lurid … ... The Maids is his first original UK production. And the question begged is: are all Kip Williams’s shows ‘like that’, in a visual sense? The answer would seem to be ‘basically, yes’. … Visually it’s loud, garish and kind of basic.

Jean Genet’s absurdist shocker gets a glib update for the TikTok era … Australian director Kip Williams radically reimagines the 1947 satire – to limited effect … Its titular skivvies serve a twentysomething billionaire mistress who puffs pineapple vapes, drapes herself in haute couture finery and cossets a labubu.

Genet’s classic The Maids is reduced to Snapchat and screeching … Kip Williams’s screen-fuelled staging of the French playwright’s psychodrama is borderline unwatchable … ... alas: even a crack cast that includes Lydia Wilson can’t prevent this souped-up take on the self-delusions of Instagram culture from feeling as though you’ve descended...
